result.topic_en: Latin notes on Riemann's Paris prize essay on heat conduction: rewriting the equation of motion, integrability conditions (curvature-type equations) for the quadratic form $\sum b_{ii'} ds_i ds_{i'}$, and the case m=1 where the form is reduced to $(a\,d\alpha + c\,d\gamma)^2 + 2m\,d\alpha\,d\beta$, with the expressions $p_{\iota,\iota'\iota''}$ and the resulting differential equations.
result.transcription:
p. 8.) Aequationem $\Delta u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ in formam redigere licet.
(a) $\Sigma_\nu p_\nu \frac{\partial q_\nu}{\partial t} = \Sigma\, T_{(\alpha,\beta)} Q(\beta,t)$
Jam [-vero-] solutiones particulares $p_1 p_2 ..$ aequationis 1., quarum numerus sit $\mu$, ita electi supponuntur, ut nulla relatio identica formae $\Sigma_\nu g_\nu p_\nu = 0$ intercedat. Quo pacto sequitur, variabili $\alpha$ semper $\mu$ valores speciales $\alpha_1 \alpha_2 .. \alpha_\mu$ attribui posse, ut determinans $\Sigma \pm p_1(\alpha_1) p_2(\alpha_2) .. p_\mu(\alpha_\mu)$ non evanescat.
Tum autem ex aequationibus e(a) prodeuntibus tribuendo $\alpha$ valores $\alpha_1 \alpha_2 .. \alpha_\mu$, expressiones quotientium differentialium $\frac{\partial q_\nu}{\partial t}$ per quotientes differentiales ipsarum $q$ secundum $\beta$ ab ipsa $\alpha$ liberae peti possunt.
p. 12.
I. $\frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota\iota''}}{\partial s_{\iota'} \partial s_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota'\iota'''}}{\partial s_\iota \partial s_{\iota''}} - \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota\iota'''}}{\partial s_{\iota'} \partial s_{\iota''}} - \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota'\iota''}}{\partial s_\iota \partial s_{\iota'''}} + \frac{1}{2B}\Sigma_{\lambda\kappa} \beta_{\lambda\kappa}(p_{\lambda,\iota'\iota'''} p_{\kappa,\iota\iota''} - p_{\lambda,\iota'\iota''} p_{\kappa,\iota\iota'''}) = 0$
p. 12 in der Linie:
$\delta' \Sigma b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'} - \delta \Sigma b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} - d \Sigma b_{\iota\iota'} \delta s_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} = 0$ \quad $2\Sigma_\iota b_{\iota\nu} d^2 s_\iota = -\Sigma_{\iota\iota'} p_{\nu\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$
$\delta' \Sigma b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'} - 2 d \Sigma b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} = 0$ \quad $2\Sigma_\iota b_{\iota\nu} d\delta s_\iota = -\Sigma_{\iota\iota'} p_{\nu\iota\iota'} ds_\iota \delta s_{\iota'}$
$\delta' \Sigma b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'} - 2\delta \Sigma b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} = 0$ \quad $2\Sigma_\iota b_{\iota\nu} \delta\delta s_\iota = -\Sigma_{\iota\iota'} p_{\nu\iota\iota'} \delta s_\iota \delta s_{\iota'}$
p. 13. In sequentibus calculos ad confirmandas has propositiones necessarios, e quibus quae supersunt {+quoad facere+} [-quam aptius[?]-] potuimus, in integrum restituere conati sumus.
I. m = 1. In hoc casu habetur forma
$\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & c \\ a' & b' & c' \end{pmatrix}$
ubi a' b' sunt functiones lineares ipsius $\gamma$ [-et-] $c'$ a $\gamma$ [-?-] independens. Tum[?] eius determinans
$\begin{vmatrix} 0 & c' & b' \\ c' & 0 & a' \\ b' & a' & c \end{vmatrix} = 2a'b'c' - cc'c'$
constans esse debet. Huius formae adjuncta haec est:
$-(a'd\alpha + b'd\beta - c'd\gamma)^2 + 2(2a'b' - cc')\, d\alpha\, d\beta$
in qua $2a'b' - cc'$ a $\gamma$ non pendet. Jam facile perspicitur, introducendo loco $\gamma$ functionem linearem ipsius $\gamma$ tamquam novam variabilem, illam formam transformari in hanc:
$(a\,d\alpha + c\,d\gamma)^2 + 2m\,d\alpha\,d\beta$
[-ubi-] in qua $a$ est functio linearis ipsius $\gamma$, $c$ et $m$ a $\gamma$ non pendent. Jam conditiones inveniendae sunt ut haec forma $g$ transformari possit in alteram, ac constantibus coefficientibus gaudentem, sive in formam $dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$. Hunc in finem primo formemus expressiones $p_{\iota,\iota'\iota''}$, quae formam sequentem induunt:
$p_{1,11} = \frac{\partial a^2}{\partial \alpha}$ \quad $p_{1,22} = 2\frac{\partial m}{\partial \beta}$ \quad $p_{1,33} = 2\frac{\partial ac}{\partial \gamma} - \frac{\partial c^2}{\partial \alpha}$ \quad $p_{1,23} = \frac{\partial ac}{\partial \beta}$ \quad $p_{1,31} = \frac{\partial a^2}{\partial \gamma}$ \quad $p_{1,12} = \frac{\partial a^2}{\partial \beta}$
$p_{2,11} = 2\frac{\partial m}{\partial \alpha} - \frac{\partial a^2}{\partial \beta}$ \quad $p_{2,22} = 0$ \quad $p_{2,33} = -\frac{\partial c^2}{\partial \beta}$ \quad $p_{2,23} = 0$ \quad $p_{2,31} = -\frac{\partial ac}{\partial \beta}$ \quad $p_{2,12} = 0$
$p_{3,11} = 2\frac{\partial ac}{\partial \alpha} - \frac{\partial a^2}{\partial \gamma}$ \quad $p_{3,22} = 0$ \quad $p_{3,33} = 0$ \quad $p_{3,23} = \frac{\partial c^2}{\partial \beta}$ \quad $p_{3,31} = \frac{\partial c^2}{\partial \alpha}$ \quad $p_{3,12} = \frac{\partial ac}{\partial \beta}$
Porro aequationes $(\iota\iota', \iota''\iota''') = 0$ (p. ..) ita exhibentur:
(11) [-$m\frac{\partial^2 c^2}{\partial \beta^2} = 2c^2$-] $m\frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial \beta^2} - \frac{\partial c}{\partial \beta}\frac{\partial m}{\partial \beta} = 0$
(22) $mc\left(\frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial \alpha^2} - \frac{\partial^2 a}{\partial \alpha \partial \gamma}\right) + \left(\frac{\partial a}{\partial \gamma} - \frac{\partial c}{\partial \alpha}\right)\left(c\frac{\partial m}{\partial \alpha} + m\frac{\partial a}{\partial \gamma}\right) = 0$
(33) $2mc\left(\frac{\partial^2 a}{\partial \beta^2} - 2\frac{\partial^2 m}{\partial \alpha \partial \beta}\right) + 2c\frac{\partial m}{\partial \beta}\left(\frac{\partial m}{\partial \alpha} - a\frac{\partial a}{\partial \beta}\right) - \frac{m}{c}\left(\frac{\partial ac}{\partial \beta}\right)^2 = 0$
(23) $2mc\left(\frac{\partial^2 ac}{\partial \beta \partial \gamma} - \frac{\partial^2 ac}{\partial \alpha \partial \beta}\right) + 4m\frac{\partial c}{\partial \beta}\left(a\left(\frac{\partial c}{\partial \alpha} - \frac{\partial a}{\partial \gamma}\right) + c\frac{\partial a}{\partial \alpha}\right) + 2c\left(c\frac{\partial a}{\partial \beta} - a\frac{\partial c}{\partial \beta}\right)\left(\frac{\partial m}{\partial \alpha} - a\frac{\partial a}{\partial \beta}\right)$
$- 2m\frac{\partial c}{\partial \alpha}\frac{\partial ac}{\partial \beta} + a\frac{\partial ac}{\partial \beta}\left(c\frac{\partial a}{\partial \beta} - a\frac{\partial c}{\partial \beta}\right) = 0$
(13) $2mc\frac{\partial^2 ac}{\partial \beta^2} - 2c\frac{\partial ac}{\partial \beta}\frac{\partial m}{\partial \beta} - 2m\frac{\partial c}{\partial \beta}\frac{\partial ac}{\partial \beta} = 0$
(12) $2m\left(2c\frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial \alpha \partial \beta} - \frac{\partial^2 ac}{\partial \beta \partial \gamma}\right) + \left(c\frac{\partial a}{\partial \beta} - a\frac{\partial c}{\partial \beta}\right)^2 = 0$
$\frac{\partial ac}{\partial \beta} - 2a\frac{\partial c}{\partial \beta}$
$\frac{\partial \frac{\partial ac}{\partial \beta}}{\partial \beta} = \frac{c\frac{\partial m}{\partial \beta} + m\frac{\partial c}{\partial \beta}}{mc}$ \quad $\frac{\partial l\, mc}{\partial \beta}$
$\frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial \alpha \partial \beta} = f''$
$+ f f'' + \frac{4(\alpha)}{f^2} f'^2$
$\frac{f^3 f''}{f'} = -4c$

items.quote: Quo pacto sequitur, variabili $\alpha$ semper $\mu$ valores speciales $\alpha_1 \alpha_2 .. \alpha_\mu$ attribui posse, ut determinans $\Sigma \pm p_1(\alpha_1) p_2(\alpha_2) .. p_\mu(\alpha_\mu)$ non evanescat.
items.english: From this it follows that one can always assign to the variable α μ special values α1...αμ such that the determinant does not vanish.

items.quote: In sequentibus calculos ad confirmandas has propositiones necessarios, e quibus quae supersunt {+quoad facere+} [-quam aptius[?]-] potuimus, in integrum restituere conati sumus.
items.english: In what follows we have tried to restore in full, as far as we could, the calculations needed to confirm these propositions, from what remains of them.

items.quote: Jam facile perspicitur, introducendo loco $\gamma$ functionem linearem ipsius $\gamma$ tamquam novam variabilem, illam formam transformari in hanc:
items.english: It is easily seen that, introducing instead of γ a linear function of γ as new variable, that form is transformed into this one.

items.quote: Jam conditiones inveniendae sunt ut haec forma $g$ transformari possit in alteram, ac constantibus coefficientibus gaudentem, sive in formam $dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$.
items.english: Now conditions must be found so that this form can be transformed into another one with constant coefficients, i.e. into the form dx²+dy²+dz².
